sanskrit: ā cyāvayasyūtaye evā hi vīra stavate sadāvṛdhaḥ astamarvanta āśavostaṃ nityāso vājina iṣaṃ stotṛbhya ā bhara
english: You stir him on for our aid — yea, the hero is praised as one ever-increasing in strength. To him the swift horses hasten home; those ever-ready coursers bring nourishment here for the singers of praise.

sanskrit: yudhmaṃ santamanarvāṇaṃ somapāmanapacyutam . naramavāryakratum indra sthātarharīṇāṃ na kiṣṭe pūrvyastutim . udānaṃśa śavasā na bhandanā agnirhi vājinaṃ viśe dadāti viśvacarṣaṇiḥ . agnī rāye svābhuvaṃ sa prīto yāti vāryamiṣaṃ stotṛbhya ā bhara
english: He who is warlike, unrivalled, a drinker of soma, unshaken — O Indra, driver of the bay steeds, the ancient praise reaches you alone. He who by his might has made the shout resound like a roar — Agni, beholder of all people, grants strength to the tribe. Agni, self-born for wealth, goes pleased to what is desirable; bring nourishment here for the singers of praise.

sanskrit: śikṣā ṇa indra rāya ā puru vidvāṃ ṛcīṣama . avā naḥ pārye dhane taṃ vo vājānāṃ patimahūmahi śravasyavaḥ . aprāyubhirjñebhirvāvṛdhenyam so agniryo vasurgṛṇe saṃ yamāyanti dhenavaḥ . samarvanto raghudruvaḥ saṃ sujātāsaḥ sūraya iṣaṃ stotṛbhya ā bhara
english: Bestow on us wealth abundantly, O Indra, you who are all-knowing, excelling in hymns — aid us at the decisive contest. We who seek glory call upon him, the lord of strength-prizes. That Agni whom I praise as the giver of good things — him the cows approach together; the swift coursers stream toward him, the nobly-born illumined sages come together; bring nourishment here for the singers of praise.

sanskrit: vajraṃ śiśāti dhiṣaṇā vareṇyam devatrā havyamūhiṣe yathā cinno abodhayaḥ satyaśravasi vāyye sujāte aśvasūnṛte
english: Wisdom sharpens the excellent thunderbolt; you carry the oblation to the gods. Just as you have awakened us — O Dawn of true fame, worthy of worship, nobly born, enriched with horses and joyous song.

sanskrit: tava dyaurindra pauṃsyaṃ pṛthivī vardhati śravaḥ . tvāmāpaḥ parvatāsaśca hinvire vibhūtarātiṃ vipra citraśociṣamagnimīḍiṣva yanturam . asya medhasya somyasya sobhare premadhvarāya pūrvyam yā sunīthe śaucadrathe vyauccho duhitardivaḥ . sā vyuccha sahīyasi satyaśravasi vāyye sujāte aśvasūnṛte
english: Heaven proclaims your heroic might, O Indra; earth magnifies your glory. The waters and the mountains spur you on — you whose bounty spreads wide. O sage, praise Agni of brilliant radiance, the controller; for this soma sacrifice, for the ancient rite of lovely ceremony — you who on the shining chariot has illumined rightly, O daughter of heaven, shine forth now, O powerful one, of true fame, worthy of worship, nobly born, enriched with horses and joyous song.

sanskrit: tvāṃ viṣṇurbṛhankṣayo mitro gṛṇāti varuṇaḥ . tvāṃ śardho madatyanu mārutam sā no adyābharadvasurvyucchā duhitardivaḥ . yo vyaucchaḥ sahīyasi satyaśravasi yāyye sujāte aśvasūnṛte
english: You Viṣṇu of great dwelling praises, Mitra praises, Varuṇa praises. The Marut host rejoices in you and follows. Let her bring us good things today — shine forth, O daughter of heaven. She who has shone forth, O powerful one, of true fame, worthy of journey, nobly born, enriched with horses and joyous song.

sanskrit: amairamitramardaya jano na puri camvorviśaddhariḥ sado vaneṣu dadhriṣe stotā vāmaśvināvṛṣi stomebhirbhūṣati prati mādhvī mama śrutaṃ havam
english: Crush the arrogant foe; as a man enters a stronghold, the tawny one enters the pressing vessels, bold in his seat amid the forests. The praiser, O Aśvins, adorns you mighty ones with hymns — O honey-sweet ones, hear my call.

sanskrit: kuvitsu no gaviṣṭaye 'gne saṃveṣiṣo rayim . urukṛduru ṇaskṛdhi sa māmṛje tiro aṇvāni meṣyo mīḍvāntsaptirna vājayuḥ . anumādyaḥ pavamāno manīṣibhiḥ somo viprebhirṛkvabhiḥ atyāyātamaśvinā tiro viśvā ahaṃ sanā . dasrā hiraṇyavarttanī suṣumṇā sindhuvāhasā mādhvī mama śrutaṃ havam
english: Will you not, O Agni, gather riches for us in our search for cattle? You who make wide space, make wide space for us. He has cleansed himself through the narrow passages — the ram-like soma, bountiful as a prize-winning steed. The flowing one, Soma purified, is to be praised by the wise, by the inspired with their hymns. Come now, O Aśvins, past all the ancient times; O wondrous ones of golden paths, gracious bearers across the river — O honey-sweet ones, hear my call.

sanskrit: mā no agne mahādhane parā vargbhārabhṛdyathā . saṃvargaṃ saṃ rayiṃ jaya ā no ratnāni bibhratāvaśvinā gacchataṃ yuvam . rudrā hiraṇyavarttanī juṣāṇā vājinīvasū mādhvī mama śrutaṃ havam
english: Do not pass us by, O Agni, when great treasure is at stake, like one bearing a heavy load aside. Conquer the spoil, gather in the wealth. O Aśvins, you two who carry gems, come to us! O Rudras of golden paths, enjoying gifts, O lords with riches and strength — O honey-sweet ones, hear my call.

sanskrit: samudrāyeva sindhavaḥ tasmā u adya savane sutaṃ bharā nūnaṃ bhūṣata śrute yahvā iva pra vayāmujjihānāḥ pra bhānavaḥ sasrate nākamaccha
english: As rivers flow to the ocean, so bring to him at today's pressing the soma that has been pressed — adorn him now, O glorified one. Like great fires springing up with their flames, the rays stream forth to the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: vi cidvṛtrasya dodhataḥ śiro bibheda vṛṣṇinā . vajreṇa śataparvaṇā vṛkaścidasya vāraṇa urāmathirā vayuneṣu bhūṣati . semaṃ na stomaṃ jujuṣāṇa ā gahīndra pra citrayā dhiyā abodhi hotā yajathāya devānūrdhvo agniḥ sumanāḥ prātarasthāt . samiddhasya ruśadadarśi pājo mahāndevastamaso niramoci
english: He cleft even the head of the roaring Vṛtra with the virile thunderbolt of a hundred joints. Even a wolf avoids the ram — it moves among the celestial stations. Come to receive this hymn of praise, O Indra, with brilliant thought. The hotar has awakened to sacrifice for the gods; Agni has stood up erect at dawn, gracious of mind. The blazing glory of the kindled fire is seen; the great god has been freed from darkness.

sanskrit: ojastadasya titviṣa ubhe yatsamavarttayat . indraścarmeva rodasī yadīṃ gaṇasya raśanāmajīgaḥ śuciraṅkte śucibhirgobhiragniḥ . āddakṣiṇā yujyate vājayantyuttānāmūrdhvo adhayajjuhūbhiḥ
english: By his flashing might he rolled together both worlds when Indra stretched the two worlds apart like a hide, when he grasped the rope of the divine host. Pure Agni adorns himself with his pure rays of light. Then the right side is yoked, prize-winning; upright he sacrifices above with his ladles outstretched.

sanskrit: tadvāṃ ceti pra vīryam yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāyaivā rātryuṣase yonimāraik
english: That heroic deed of yours two shines forth conspicuously — as when Night, set in motion by Savitṛ's impulsion, yielded her womb to Dawn.

sanskrit: sarūpa vṛṣannā gahīmau bhadrau dhuryāvabhi . tāvimā upa sarpataḥ indrāgnī apasaspari upa pra yanti dhītayaḥ . ṛtasya pathyā anu ruśādvatsā ruśatī śvetyāgādāraigu kṛṣṇā sadanānyasyāḥ . samānabandhū amṛte anūcī dyāvā varṇaṃ carata āmināne
english: O bull, come of like form; O you two auspicious ones, come as yoke-fellows. Those two approach here — toward Indra and Agni the prayers come forth from all around. Along the paths of sacred order, the shining calf comes gleaming; the bright one has departed; the dark one goes to the seats of the other. The two sisters, immortal and following together, Heaven and Earth move through their hues in alternation.

sanskrit: nīva śīrṣāṇi mṛḍhvaṃ madhya āpasya tiṣṭhati . śṛṅgebhirdaśabhirdiśan indrāgnī taviṣāṇi vām sadhasthāni prayāṃsi ca . yuvoraptūryaṃ hitam samāno adhvā svasroranantastamanyānyā carato devaśiṣṭe . na methete na tasthatuḥ sumeke naktoṣāsā samanasā virūpe
english: Like a reed bending, they are gracious; he stands in the middle of the waters, pointing with ten horns. O Indra and Agni, your strongholds and your feasts are indeed mighty. Placed between the two of you is the ritual function; the two sisters follow the same path endlessly, the one following the other, directed by the gods. Night and Dawn, alike in mind yet of different forms, do not collide nor do they stand still together.

sanskrit: ayaṃ yaḥ puro vibhinattyojasā mandānaḥ śiprayandhasaḥ arvāñcā nūnaṃ rathyeha yātaṃ pīpivāṃsamaśvinā gharmamaccha
english: He who by his might splits the citadels asunder, exhilarated by the soma pressed through the strainer — O Aśvins, now come hitherward with your chariot to this full-swelling sacred offering.

sanskrit: dānā mṛgo na vāraṇaḥ purutrā carathaṃ dadhe . na kiṣṭvā ni yamadā sute gamo mahāṃścarasyojasā na saṃskṛtaṃ pra mimīto gamiṣṭhānti nūnamaśvinopastuteha . divābhipitvevasāgamiṣṭhā pratyavarttiṃ dāśuṣe śambhaviṣṭhā
english: Like a wild elephant giving gifts, you two wander widely to many places. None can restrain you; you come when soma is pressed — mighty you two range at will with your power. O Aśvins, none can measure what you have made ready; praised here, now do come most swiftly. At the approach of the day come most eagerly, granting return and welfare to the worshipper.

sanskrit: ya ugraḥ sannaniṣṭṛtaḥ sthiro raṇāya saṃskṛtaḥ . yadi stoturmaghavā śṛṇavaddhavaṃ nendro yoṣatyā gamat utā yātaṃ saṃgave prātarahno madhyandina uditā sūryasya . divā naktamavasā śantamena nedānīṃ pītiraśvinā tatāna
english: He who is fierce, unvanquished, firm, prepared for battle — if the bounteous Maghavan hears the singer's call, Indra will not linger with a woman and will come. And come you both at the gathering time, at the early morning, at midday when the sun has risen. By day and by night with most blissful aid — now has the drinking by the Aśvins been established.

sanskrit: abhi viśvāni kāvyā niṣkṛṇvānā āyudhānīva dhṛṣṇavaḥ prati gāvo 'ruṣīryanti mātaraḥ
english: Accomplishing all their poetic works, bold as warriors with their weapons, the ruddy cow-mothers come back in return.

sanskrit: pavamānā divasparyantarikṣādasṛkṣata . pṛthivyā adhi sānavi udapaptannaruṇā bhānavo vṛthā svāyujo aruṣīrgā ayukṣata . akrannuṣāso vayunāni pūrvathā ruśantaṃ bhānumaruṣīraśiśrayuḥ
english: The purifying ones, flowing from heaven, were poured forth from the middle air. Over the ridge of earth the ruddy rays leapt up freely; the self-yoked ruddy cows were yoked. The Dawns have cried out their signals as before; they have made the shining ray to lean upon the ruddy one.

sanskrit: pavamānāsa āśavaḥ śubhrā asṛgramindavaḥ . ghnanto viśvā apa dviṣaḥ arcanti nārīrapaso na viṣṭibhiḥ samānena yojanenā parāvataḥ . iṣaṃ vahantīḥ sukṛte sudānave viśvedaha yajamānāya sunvate
english: The purifying swift and brilliant soma-drops have been released. Striking away all enemies, the women honor them with their works and services from a common yoking in the distance. Carrying nourishment to the right-doer, to the good giver, every day they bring it to the sacrificer who presses the soma.

sanskrit: indrāgnī vājasātamā āyukṣātāmaśvinā yātave rathaṃ prāsāvīddevaḥ savitā jagatpṛthak
english: Indra and Agni, most mighty for winning the prize — the Aśvins have yoked their chariot to come; the divine Savitṛ has urged the whole world forward, each to its own place.

sanskrit: pra vāmarcantyukthino nīthāvido jaritāraḥ . indrāgnī iṣa ā vṛṇe yadyuñjāthe vṛṣaṇamaśvinā rathaṃ ghṛtena no madhunā kṣatramukṣatam . asmākaṃ brahma pṛtanāsu jinvataṃ vayaṃ dhanā śūrasātā bhajemahi
english: The chanters of lauds, knowing the sacred songs, sing your praise, O you two. I choose Indra and Agni for nourishment. When you two Aśvins yoke your bull-like chariot, sprinkle our sovereignty with ghee and honey. Quicken our prayers in battles; may we share in the prizes won by heroes.

sanskrit: indrāgnī navatiṃ puro dāsapatnīradhūnutam . sākamekena karmaṇā arvāṅtricakro madhuvāhano ratho jīrāśvo aśvinoryātu suṣṭutaḥ . trivandhuro maghavā viśvasaubhagaḥ śaṃ na ā vakṣaddvipade catuṣpade
english: Indra and Agni shook down ninety strongholds whose lord was a slave — together by a single act. Now let the chariot of the Aśvins, three-wheeled and honey-laden, drawn by swift horses, come hither well-praised. Three-felied, bounteous, possessed of all good fortune — may it bring wellbeing to us for the two-footed and the four-footed.

sanskrit: agne sasṛjmahe giraḥ acchā vājaṃ sahasriṇam
english: O Agni, we have released our songs toward you, toward the thousandfold prize.

sanskrit: upa cchāyāmiva ghṛṇeraganma śarma te vayam . agne hiraṇyasandṛśaḥ abhi priyāṇi kāvyā viśvā cakṣāṇo arṣati . haristuñjāna āyudhā
english: We have come to your shelter as to the shade of heat; we find your protection, O Agni. Golden of aspect, he flows over all the beloved poetic works, beholding them. The tawny one, wielding his weapons, presses forward.

sanskrit: ya ugra iva śaryahā tigmaśṛṅgo na vaṃsagaḥ . agne puro rurojitha sa marmṛjāna āyubhiribho rājeva suvrataḥ . śyeno na vaṃsu ṣīdati
english: Like a fierce destroyer of arrows, sharp-horned like a bull of the herd — O Agni, you have shattered the fortresses; cleansing yourself with your flames, you shine like a king of excellent ordinance. Like a falcon he settles in the treetops.

sanskrit: sa no viśvā divo vasūto pṛthivyā adhi . punāna indavā bhara
english: Bring to us all the riches of heaven, and those over the earth — O purifying soma-drops, bring them here.

sanskrit: ajasraṃ gharmamīmahe
english: We seek the inexhaustible warmth of the sacred fire.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ pratipaprathe yajñasya svaruttiran . ṛtūnutsṛjate vaśī
english: He who has spread this sacrifice abroad, passing beyond its heavenly light — the self-governing one releases the seasons.

sanskrit: agniḥ priyeṣu dhāmasu kāmo bhūtasya bhavyasya . sabhrāḍeko vi rājati
english: Agni in his beloved abodes — the desire of what has been and what shall be — shines alone in all his splendor as sovereign.
